title: Hyperkalaemia: acute management (adult)
subject: nephrology
setting: Emergency department, ward, ICU, dialysis unit
summary: Protect the heart with IV calcium when the ECG shows changes, shift potassium into cells with insulin-glucose and nebulised salbutamol, remove potassium with binders or dialysis, and monitor glucose closely to prevent hypoglycaemia (UKKA 2023).

sections.title: Recognise and classify
items: Severity (UKKA 2023): mild 5.5 to 5.9 mmol/L, moderate 6.0 to 6.4 mmol/L, severe 6.5 mmol/L or more.
ECG changes: peaked T waves, flattened or absent P waves, broad QRS, sine wave pattern, bradycardia, ventricular tachycardia or fibrillation. A normal ECG does not exclude risk.

Causes: AKI or CKD, ACE inhibitor or ARB, spironolactone, potassium-sparing diuretics, trimethoprim, NSAIDs, heparin, potassium supplements or salt substitutes, rhabdomyolysis, tumour lysis, DKA, adrenal insufficiency.
Suspect pseudohyperkalaemia with a haemolysed or delayed sample or very high platelet or white cell counts, but never delay treatment when the ECG shows changes.

sections.title: Step 1: protect the heart
items: Potassium 6.0 mmol/L or more in hospital: urgent 12-lead ECG. Continuous cardiac monitoring for 6.5 or more, any ECG changes, or 6.0 to 6.4 in an unwell patient.
Use a point-of-care blood gas potassium while the laboratory result is awaited.

ECG changes present: calcium gluconate 10% 30 mL IV over 10 minutes (6.8 mmol calcium) into a large vein. In cardiac arrest or peri-arrest use calcium chloride 10% 10 mL IV over 5 minutes (bolus during CPR).
Repeat IV calcium if ECG changes persist after the first dose, or if hyperkalaemia remains refractory once its effect wears off (about 60 minutes). Calcium does not lower potassium.
Digoxin therapy is a caution for IV calcium: give slowly with continuous ECG monitoring.

sections.title: Step 2: shift potassium into cells
items: Moderate or severe: 10 units soluble (regular) insulin with 25 g glucose IV over 5 to 15 minutes into a large vein. 25 g glucose = 50 mL of 50%, 100 mL of 25%, 125 mL of 20% or 250 mL of 10%.
Check blood glucose before insulin. If pre-treatment glucose is below 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L), follow with 10% glucose at 50 mL/h for 5 hours (25 g).
Monitor glucose at 0, 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 300 and 360 minutes; target 72 to 126 mg/dL (4.0 to 7.0 mmol/L) and treat hypoglycaemia below 72 mg/dL (4.0 mmol/L) promptly.
Salbutamol 10 to 20 mg nebulised as an adjunct for severe (and optionally moderate) hyperkalaemia; never as monotherapy. Use 10 mg with ischaemic heart disease or tachyarrhythmia.
If potassium is still 6.0 mmol/L or more 2 hours after insulin-glucose, or rebounds, consider a further dose and seek specialist advice.
IV sodium bicarbonate is not used routinely for acute hyperkalaemia.

sections.title: Step 3: remove potassium
items: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) 10 g orally three times daily for up to 72 hours for severe hyperkalaemia; consider it for moderate hyperkalaemia.
Patiromer 8.4 g orally once daily is an option for potassium 6.0 mmol/L or more; separate from other oral drugs by 3 hours.
Calcium resonium is no longer routinely recommended for acute hyperkalaemia; where newer binders are unavailable it acts slowly and must not replace insulin-glucose or dialysis.
Stop contributing drugs (potassium supplements, RAS inhibitors, MRAs, NSAIDs, trimethoprim) and treat the cause: relieve obstruction, restore volume, treat DKA or adrenal crisis.

sections.title: Dialysis and referral
items: Haemodialysis patients with potassium 6.5 mmol/L or more need urgent dialysis; give IV calcium for ECG changes even if dialysis is immediately available, and standard medical therapy while it is arranged.
Refer severe hyperkalaemia to the renal or critical care team, especially if it persists after initial treatment, with oligo-anuric AKI, rhabdomyolysis or tumour lysis.
Cardiac arrest: follow the ALS hyperkalaemia pathway, with calcium chloride 10% 10 mL IV bolus and insulin-glucose.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: Serum potassium at least 1, 2, 4, 6 and 24 hours after treatment of moderate or severe hyperkalaemia; expect rebound as shift therapies wear off.
Blood glucose for 6 hours after each insulin-glucose dose.
Keep cardiac monitoring while potassium is severe or ECG changes persist.

sections.title: Community and chronic hyperkalaemia
items: Community results: mild, repeat within 3 days; moderate, repeat within 1 day; severe, admit for immediate assessment and treatment.
Hyperkalaemia on RAS inhibitors in CKD or heart failure: reduce potassium (diet review, diuretic, binders) rather than stopping these drugs where possible.
Recurrent hyperkalaemia: dietary review with a renal dietitian, and ask about low-sodium salt substitutes, which usually contain potassium chloride.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Underdosing calcium gluconate: one 10 mL ampoule of 10% contains only 2.2 mmol calcium; the UKKA dose is 30 mL.
Hypoglycaemia after insulin-glucose, particularly without diabetes, with low body weight, renal failure or pre-treatment glucose below 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L).
Relying on salbutamol alone, or repeating shift therapy in an anuric patient instead of arranging dialysis.
Extravasation of 50% glucose or calcium through a small peripheral cannula.

drugs.name: Calcium gluconate 10%
drugs.notes: For ECG changes; repeat if changes persist. 10 mL contains 2.2 mmol calcium.

drugs.name: Calcium chloride 10%
drugs.dose: 10 mL IV over 5 minutes (bolus in cardiac arrest)
drugs.notes: Preferred in arrest or peri-arrest; irritant, use a large or central vein.

drugs.name: Soluble insulin with glucose
drugs.dose: 10 units soluble insulin IV with 25 g glucose over 5 to 15 minutes
drugs.notes: Then 10% glucose 50 mL/h for 5 hours if pre-treatment glucose is below 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L). Monitor glucose for 6 hours.

drugs.name: Salbutamol
drugs.notes: Adjunct only; 10 mg in ischaemic heart disease.

drugs.name: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC)
drugs.dose: 10 g orally three times daily for up to 72 hours
drugs.notes: Maintenance 5 g once daily, titrated between 10 g daily and 5 g on alternate days. May cause oedema and hypokalaemia.

drugs.name: Patiromer
drugs.notes: Maximum 25.2 g daily. Separate other oral drugs by 3 hours; can cause hypomagnesaemia and constipation.
